\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أقام} (aqāma)}{أقام (aqāma)}]{\ar{أقام} (aqāma) — to hold an event; to reside}

\label{lesson:AR-C328-aqama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for until, then the Arabic for throughout.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أقام}}
\textbf{\ar{أقام}} — \emph{aqāma} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold an event; to reside\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أقامت} \ar{المدرسة} \ar{حفلا} \ar{في} \ar{نهاية} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aqāmat al-madrasa ḥaflan fī nihāyat as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school held a party at the end of the year.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقيم}, \emph{yuqīm}.

\ar{أقام} \ar{حفلا}: to throw a party. \ar{أقام} \ar{في}: to live in a place.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أقام}} (\emph{aqāma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-w-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to stand up\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{qāma}. It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to set a thing up\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}to stay\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqāma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqāma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqāmat al-madrasa ḥaflan fī nihāyat as-sana.} — The school held a party at the end of the year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for until, then the Arabic for throughout, then say \emph{aqāma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أقام} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hold an event; to reside\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أحيا} (aḥyā)}{أحيا (aḥyā)}]{\ar{أحيا} (aḥyā) — to perform at; to revive}

\label{lesson:AR-C328-ahya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for throughout, then the Arabic for to hold an event.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أحيا}}
\textbf{\ar{أحيا}} — \emph{aḥyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to perform at; to revive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أحيا} \ar{المطرب} \ar{حفل} \ar{العرس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aḥyā al-muṭrib ḥafl al-ʿurs.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The singer performed at the wedding party.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحيي}, \emph{yuḥyī}.

\ar{أحيا} \ar{حفلا}: a singer performs at a party. \ar{أحيا} \ar{ذكرى}: to mark an anniversary.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أحيا}} (\emph{aḥyā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-y-y} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to live\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{ḥayāh}, life, and of the taught \emph{ḥayawān}, an animal. It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to give life to\textquotedblright{}: to bring a night or a memory to life.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḥyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḥyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḥyā al-muṭrib ḥafl al-ʿurs.} — The singer performed at the wedding party.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for throughout, then the Arabic for to hold an event, then say \emph{aḥyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أحيا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To perform at; to revive\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{موكب} (mawkib)}{موكب (mawkib)}]{\ar{موكب} (mawkib) — a procession}

\label{lesson:AR-C328-mawkib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to hold an event, then the Arabic for to perform at.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{موكب}}
\textbf{\ar{موكب}} — \emph{mawkib} — \textquotedblleft{}a procession\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مر} \ar{موكب} \ar{العرس} \ar{في} \ar{الشارع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marra mawkib al-ʿurs fī ash-shāriʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The wedding procession went down the street.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{مواكب}, \emph{mawākib}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{موكب}} (\emph{mawkib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-k-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to walk along in a grave, leisurely way\textquotedblright{}. A \emph{mawkib} is a company moving at that pace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawkib}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marra mawkib al-ʿurs fī ash-shāriʿ.} — The wedding procession went down the street.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to hold an event, then the Arabic for to perform at, then say \emph{mawkib} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وليمة} (walīma)}{وليمة (walīma)}]{\ar{وليمة} (walīma) — a banquet, a feast}

\label{lesson:AR-C328-walima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to perform at, then the Arabic for a procession.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وليمة}}
\textbf{\ar{وليمة}} — \emph{walīma} — \textquotedblleft{}a banquet, a feast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طبخت} \ar{النساء} \ar{الطعام} \ar{للوليمة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭabakhat an-nisāʾ aṭ-ṭaʿām li-l-walīma.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The women cooked the food for the banquet.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وليمة}} (\emph{walīma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-l-m} (Lane), where \emph{walīma} is first the feast made for a wedding, and then for any occasion.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{walīma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{walīma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭabakhat an-nisāʾ aṭ-ṭaʿām li-l-walīma.} — The women cooked the food for the banquet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to perform at, then the Arabic for a procession, then say \emph{walīma} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مدعو} (madʿuww)}{مدعو (madʿuww)}]{\ar{مدعو} (madʿuww) — an invited guest}

\label{lesson:AR-C328-maduww}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a procession, then the Arabic for a banquet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مدعو}}
\textbf{\ar{مدعو}} — \emph{madʿuww} — \textquotedblleft{}an invited guest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{كل} \ar{مدعو} \ar{يحمل} \ar{هدية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna kull madʿuww yaḥmilu hadiyya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every guest was carrying a present.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{مدعوون}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مدعو}} (\emph{madʿuww}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-ʿ-w} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to call, to invite\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{daʿā}. \emph{Madʿuww} is the one called: an invited guest.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{madʿuww}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna kull madʿuww yaḥmilu hadiyya.} — Every guest was carrying a present.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a procession, then the Arabic for a banquet, then say \emph{madʿuww} again
\end{itemize}
